Author: Husk & Bone
Name: LE-C UI
Description:
LE-C UI (Limsa E-Couple UI) draws the game's HUD again in a look of your choosing: usual, cute (pastels, hearts and sparkles, round corners; six colour sets) or edgy (black, sharp corners, slashes, capitals; six colour sets), each with your own colours, corners, border and little drawings.

Each piece of the HUD has its own switch: the chat box, the party list, the duty list (quests, the duty, FATEs, the duty finder), the job gauge as the game has it (every job's gauge windows, the second one its own piece too), your HP and MP (with your MP's number), your target and its target, your focus target (right-click either for the game's own menu), your cast bar, your statuses, the enemy list, the limit gauge and the experience bar. Switched on, LE-C UI draws that piece where the game's own is in your HUD layout and keeps the game's own off the screen; switched off, the game's own is back exactly where it was. Nothing of the game's settings is ever changed: your HUD layouts, configuration, chat settings and keybinds stay exactly as they are, the game's own pieces come back by themselves while the HUD layout editor is open, when you log out and when LE-C UI is disabled, and each update keeps a copy of your LE-C UI settings.

Every piece is a box over the game that's moved and sized the same way (/lecui place, or the arrows on the settings window's title bar, shows them all: drag one, or its sides; it snaps to the others and the screen's edges; hold Ctrl to move them all together), with how solid its background is, how strongly it's drawn, the shadow under its writing and its size each its own setting. When the game's own menus and questions open over a piece, it fades out of their way. Borders can be switched off for one piece or all of them. A piece shows when the game would show its own (hidden in cutscenes, by your HUD layout, and so on).

The party list has everyone's HP and MP with their numbers, the game's job icons (or its framed ones, or the roles), your chocobo's icon, the party's numbers, the leader's crown, the signs over heads, ready check answers, who has the enemy's attention, who's raising whom, the icon of what each member is casting and a mark for what Esuna takes off; it targets on click, opens the game's own menu on right-click and is a mouseover target for your macros. The chat box has its own tabs, your chat colours (the game's, or a colour of your own for any channel: start from the Pastel or Neon set), its own colours for its background, edge, tabs, times and the line you type in, names in colours of your choosing (one colour, a colour for each person, or a colour of their own for people you pick), clickable links (map flags, names, other plugins' links), the game's own menu for a name you right-click, your last lines on Up and Down, a button that opens the tells window (with how many tells are unread), and opens when you press Enter, as the game's does; drag its tab row to move it any time (its sides and corner size it only while the pieces are being moved and sized: /lecui place). The duty list opens a quest in the journal on click.

Saved chat (on from the start, kept for good; switch it off or pick a shorter time on the Chat box page): your tells, and any other channels you pick, are kept in a text file a day on your computer, never sent anywhere; /lecui history reads them back with a search.

Tells window (on from the start; switch it off on the Chat box page): your tells in a window of their own, a conversation for each person with a line to answer on, popping up when one comes in (after a fight or a cutscene, not during); History on a conversation opens every saved tell with that person.

/lecui opens the settings; /lecui place shows, moves and sizes every piece; /lecui history opens saved chat; /lecui tells opens the tells window; /lecui on|off <piece|all>; /lecui usual|cute|edgy.
Punchline: The game's HUD drawn again in your look: the chat box, party list, duty list, job gauges, target and the rest, usual, cute or edgy.
